chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Abu al-Maghra', from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'The heart is such that during a time from the night and the day, there is neither faith in it nor disbelief. Do you not find that to be so? Then after that, a spot from Allah appears in the heart of His servant with whatever He wills. If He wills, [He places] faith, and if He wills, [He places] disbelief.'

key_terms.الْقَلْبُ: The heart, considered the spiritual center of belief and intellect
key_terms.عَبْدِهِ: His servant, referring to the human being under divine authority
key_terms.نُكْتَةٌ: A spot, mark, or point, indicating a decisive divine placement or change in state

ai.seo_question: What is the state of the heart between faith and disbelief according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the dynamic nature of the heart (qalb), illustrating its fluctuation between states of faith and disbelief, which aligns with the Shia concept of the heart's susceptibility to divine influence. The 'spot' (nuqtah) signifies a decisive moment of divine decree or spiritual realization that solidifies the heart's orientation, reflecting the interplay between human potentiality and Allah's will. This concept is often discussed in the context of spiritual purification (tazkiyah) and the conditions under which faith becomes firmly rooted in the believer's heart.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Abu Al Magra’a, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘

I heard himasws saying: ‘The الْقَلْبُ (Qalb) happens to be such during a time from the night and the day, there is neither Emān in it nor Kufr (disbelief). But, do you not find that (to be so)? Then a spot appears after that from Allahazwj in the heart of Hisazwj servant with whatever Heazwj so Desires. If Heazwj so Desires with Emān, and if Heazwj so Desires, with Kufr (disbelief)’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Yunus from abu al- Maghra’ from abu Basir who has said the following:

“I heard abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) saying, ‘The heart in (certain) hours of the night and day has no belief or disbelief in it. Do you not find that in yourself? Thereafter, a dot from Allah comes in the heart of His servant in the form that He wills. If He wills, it is with belief and if He wills, it is in disbelief.’”
